question_en: What are the name, manufacturer, and specific version of the instrument in the figure?
answer: Jastrow Memory Apparatus; C. H. Stoelting; All-Metal Improved Model
gold_trajectory:
# Detailed Simulated Search Trajectory · P2-2-2-B02

## Step 01 · Accessing psychological experiment instrument data from the screen panel and rear mechanical parts

**Action:** Record the current input screen panel, openings, and base; use `historical psychology apparatus vertical screen memory`, `memory apparatus tachistoscope metal screen`, etc., as search examples.

**Evidence Observation:** The instrument is a slender upright board with two horizontal guide rails in the middle section, holding an insert with two small openings; wheels, rods, and control components are visible at the lower right rear, and the base has short, thick outward-extending feet. Most of the front is obscured by an intact panel, supporting the hypothesis that it is an experimental device for presenting visual stimuli. Photo color alone cannot prove "all-metal," and the two holes could also be a configuration for interchangeable inserts, so they cannot be presumed as fixed features of the entire series in advance.

**Result of this step:** Take the memory presenter and tachistoscope as search directions; specific names, manufacturers, and versions all require catalog evidence.

## Step 02 · Locating identical physical objects in university catalogs

**Action:** Check the `Memory Apparatus, Jastrow's, improved form` entry in the long page of National Taiwan University's historical psychological instruments, and open the original photo for that entry.

https://homepage.ntu.edu.tw/~linth/index.102.htm

https://homepage.ntu.edu.tw/~linth/index.53.jpg

**Evidence Observation:** The original photo of the entry corresponds to the input: the positions of the slender screen panel, the front double-small-hole insert, the lower-right rear control mechanism, and the short thick base feet are the same. The corresponding text lists Jastrow, Stoelting, and `No.21105`, and introduces the improved model. Since this page contains various experimental instruments, the text must be matched to its belonging image; one cannot apply the manufacturer or principle of neighboring entries to the target.

**Result of this step:** Clues for Jastrow Memory Apparatus, C. H. Stoelting, and the improved model have been obtained; since the question specifically requests the version, continue to verify the basis for "all-metal" in the original manufacturer's catalog.

## Step 03 · Confirming version and front/back construction using the original manufacturer's catalog

**Action:** Read entry `21105` on page 91 of the 1930 C. H. Stoelting catalog preserved by Virtual Laboratory, and check the front and back views of the same number on page 92.

https://vlp-new.ur.de/record/lit13685/export/json

https://digilib.mpiwg-berlin.mpg.de/digitallibrary/servlet/Scaler?fn=/permanent/vlp/lit13685/pages/p0091&dw=1800&dh=2400

https://digilib.mpiwg-berlin.mpg.de/digitallibrary/servlet/Scaler?fn=/permanent/vlp/lit13685/pages/p0092&dw=1800&dh=2400

**Evidence Observation:** Page 91 explicitly states `Memory Apparatus, Jastrow's; improved form`, explaining the change from an old wooden version to an all-metal structure, mounted on a heavy iron base, with an aluminum screen panel featuring horizontal guide slots, and the card holder and control actions located at the back. The insert guide rails in the front view on page 92, the lower lifting card mechanism in the back view, and the outward-extending base correspond to the side-front perspective in the question image. The front and back views together explain why the question image simultaneously reveals the front insert and the lower-right rear rod components. The bottom of this page contains text for other devices continuing from the previous page's `21113`; one cannot automatically attribute its automatic card-feeding parameters to `21105`.

**Result of this step:** The instrument name, manufacturer, and "All-Metal Improved Model" are all directly supported by original manufacturer text and construction details; the catalog number serves only as a positioning aid.

## Step 04 · Distinguishing the old Jastrow version from similar vertical tachistoscopes

**Action:** Compare with the old-style memory apparatus in Figure 57 on page 202 of Titchener's 1902 manual, then examine the actual text and images for Wundt's falling-screen tachistoscope and the Musée Bourdon guillotine-style tachistoscope.

https://vlp-new.ur.de/record/lit11937/export/json

https://digilib.mpiwg-berlin.mpg.de/digitallibrary/servlet/Scaler?fn=/permanent/vlp/lit11937/pages/p0202&dw=1800&dh=2400

https://www.aspi.unimib.it/it/data/entita/226-tachistoscopio-a-caduta-di-wundt

https://aspi.archivio.com/cataloga/media/collectiveaccess/images/1/1/6/5/90494_ca_object_representations_media_116597_large.jpg

https://www.lp3c.fr/activites-scientifiques/musee-bourdon/tachistoscope-guillotine

https://www.lp3c.fr/system/files/LP3C/MUSEE-BOURDON/Tachistoscope-a-guillotine-v2.jpg

**Evidence Observation:** The closest old-style Jastrow also has an upright screen panel and small windows, but Figure 57 clearly draws a large front flip-down shutter and two curved sled feet extending forward and backward connected by a crossbar; the target and the original manufacturer's improved model figure have a flat screen panel, insert guide slots, and short thick outward-extending feet. Wundt images and text feature a large top pulley, double coils, and an open stand, which do not correspond to the question image's enclosed straight board. The Bourdon physical object's back view has upper and lower card-feeding rollers, a middle rotating arm, and a hanging counterweight; the target catalog uses a lifting card holder, with exposed control components concentrated at the bottom. These comparisons support the specific version judgment and are not derived from inferring the same instrument merely because "all are used for short-term visual presentation".

**Result of this step:** Old versions within the same family and similar tachistoscopes with images have been distinguished with evidence; there is no need to expand to all historical psychological instruments.

## Step 05 · Writing the name, manufacturer, and version completely into the answer

**Action:** Summarize the common conclusions from the university physical object entry and the original manufacturer's catalog, adopting the three items of information required by the question.

**Evidence Observation:** `No.21105` is a catalog item number rather than a single-unit serial number; 1930 is the year of the catalog read and cannot be used to determine that the instrument in the image was produced in 1930. Differences in the small-hole configuration caused by interchangeable inserts also do not affect the identity as the All-Metal Improved Model.

**Result of this step:** Evidence for the name, manufacturer, and version is sufficient; stop searching.

**Formal Answer:**

Jastrow Memory Apparatus; C. H. Stoelting; All-Metal Improved Model
